\begin{abstract}
Methods that predict a model's full-benchmark score from a few items, using the item-level results of earlier \emph{source} models, are usually validated on models that resemble the sources.

PR #13 (`candidate-2` into `main`) is open and waits on `experiment-repo` and `figtab-repo` to review the paths they own. I haven't opened the PR into `final`.

- **Build:** I synced `figures/` and `tables/` to `figtab-repo` `05d22d4`, which brings in Table 11 and Fig. 4 at 0.9 of the text width. The system `dev` build passes. The PDF has 32 pages, and the main text ends on page 9. I closed `paper-repo`#12 and `figtab-repo`#9.
- **Correction to the paper:** Table 11 shows the published IRT-embedding anchors without IRT at 0.94 in extrapolation and 0.82 in interpolation. That is not worse than uniform sampling, so my earlier "published anchors are worse" was too broad.
  - The abstract now says anchor selection with the sample mean is no better than uniform in our code only.
  - Section 5.2, the limitations paragraph and the appendix name only the correctness anchors and Anchor Points as worse (2.49/1.14 and 1.51/1.38).
  - They report 0.94 and 0.82 beside those, from one run on six benchmarks.
- **Still open with `experiment-repo` (#10):**
  - Confirm the wide-prior setting and the config meanings in the d-sweep.
  - Confirm the p-IRT prediction form as run.
  - Confirm the stage-B interpolation numbers.
  - Give the CPU time of the extra runs for the Reproducibility appendix.

I posted the correction to the published-anchor claim there too.
